video_title: Lou, Chandler & Boogie Debate if Wemby DISRESPECTFUL after NBA Finals Loss?!?

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' young core shows immense potential despite playoff loss
quotes.excerpt: This team is super talented. This team is on an insane trajectory.
quotes.quote: This team is super talented. This team is on an insane trajectory as well as the Oklahoma City Thunder just because of their age. We look at Jeremy Sochan and Stephon Castle and Victor Wembanyama. This is the experience that they didn't have. Now next year going into the season and the playoffs, I don't know what our excuse or reasoning for them not to be there again is because they just went through this extremely important vital experience.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's fourth-quarter performance in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: If you look at his fourth-quarter numbers in these finals, 12 of 35, two of eight.
quotes.quote: If you look at his fourth-quarter numbers in these finals, 12 of 35, two of eight from three, 13 of 18 from the free-throw line. I feel like that's a big, let's start learning there, right?

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama and the Spurs need to refine their offensive game
quotes.excerpt: He's still very raw. He's still got a lot of things to figure out.
quotes.quote: This is just a part of learning, learning this game, figuring out his spots, figuring out his go-to moves. He's still very raw. He's still got a lot of things to figure out. And it's not even just Victor Wembanyama. I think this is a lesson for the entire group. When you think about the group as a whole, from De'Aaron Fox to the last guy on the bench, I think this was a learning experience for everybody, even coach Mitch Johnson.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's offensive versatility and need for physical development
quotes.excerpt: He's so incredible and he can do so many different things.
quotes.quote: He's so incredible and he can do so many different things that we don't really give him the benefit of the doubt of being young. Now at 22 years old, he can look back on this run and this experience. He can look at film or he can know, maybe I need to get a little bigger, adjust my body, offensively find my spots where I can lean on at any point of the game where you can throw me the basketball and go get a bucket. All great offensive players, you almost know where they're going to go in the fourth quarter where their hot spots was. Jalen Brunson, either mid-block, 10-12 feet from the rim, those are his spots. Victor Wembanyama is still yet to find that based on the way that he plays. If he refines some of the things that he does on the offensive end and get a little selfish, a little greediness in his game, I think we see him turning the page again.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama must improve his efficiency to avoid settling for bad shots
quotes.excerpt: You shouldn't shoot 42% from the field being 7'5. That means you're settling taking bad outside shots.
quotes.quote: You shouldn't shoot 42% from the field being 7'5. That means you're settling taking a lot of bad outside shots.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama should model his physical development after Kevin Garnett
quotes.excerpt: A great body type for him would be like a Kevin Garnett.
quotes.quote: I don't think he needs to get bigger. I don't think he needs to add weight, just stronger. I think a great body type for him would be like a Kevin Garnett. Kevin Garnett wasn't the biggest guy, but he was super strong, he was wiry, but he was still in his slim frame. So I think that would be ideal for Victor Wembanyama as far as where he wants to go with his body.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks fans criticize Wembanyama for not shaking hands after series
quotes.excerpt: It appeared Victor Wembanyama didn't shake the hands of the Knicks afterwards.
quotes.quote: It appeared Victor Wembanyama didn't shake the hands of the Knicks afterwards and now we don't like that. It's arrogant, he's a bad guy. A lot of Knicks fans are doing that to whom I respond, go burn something else down and maybe not worry about what's classy and what's not.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Everything is scrutinized when playing on the world stage
quotes.excerpt: When you're on the world stage, you're on the biggest stage, everything is going to get dissected.
quotes.quote: When you're on the world stage, you're on the biggest stage, everything is going to get dissected. And he's had a couple different things that we've paid attention to, personality or competitive style-wise where we were like, oh, we didn't know he had that. We didn't know he had a little asshole in his system. So when he introduced us to it, game after game after game, I think people were a little taking aback. Now as far as the handshaking thing, we can't give him an excuse or give the rest of that team excuses like that. Hard-fought battles, everybody knows it's to shake hands, you congratulate your opponent, and you move on with it. He doesn't have to be overly, but obviously you saw Jalen Brunson heading over to shake his hand, he beelines out. All of these things are going to be under a microscope.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Star players have a professional responsibility to handle media and losses
quotes.excerpt: You are the next man up, you are going to be the face of this league.
quotes.quote: You are Victor Wembanyama, all eyes are on you. You are the next man up, you are going to be the face of this league. Everyone is watching what you do and how you react. So given his postseason and all the stuff he's been through with the flagrant fouls and being one away from missing media, as a star player especially, you have a responsibility to do these certain things. Whether that's media after a loss, after a game, after missing a game-winner, whatever it is, you have to be a professional.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's behavior is a learning moment for a young player
quotes.excerpt: Let's not take away the fact that this is a 22-year-old kid.
quotes.quote: Let's not take away the fact that this is a 22-year-old kid. We've all done young, immature things as far as how we handle losses that we go through. So when I sit there and see a moment like that, one, I didn't take it as the most negative thing. Yeah, he could have stayed back, shook hands, but it's also where the Knicks are about to celebrate their moment. So you kind of get out of the way.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Reputation building comes with increased scrutiny for young stars
quotes.excerpt: As he builds his reputation, everything that we keep saying is, he's 22.
quotes.quote: As he builds his reputation, everything that we keep saying is, he's 22. It can't be that, it can't be that. He's not the first person to not shake hands. But check this out, no, check me out though. We probably said bad things about the other guys that didn't shake hands. We can't say that about the, we can't say all of this. We can't make the same excuse about the flagrant fouls, we can't make the excuse about the media availability, we can't make the excuse about see y'all never, we can't make the excuse about not shaking hands. At some point, you just got to put it in a pot. And if he not, if he not with it, let's just say he not with it. Let's put him in the group of guys that we love to criticize about the same exact things. That's all I'm, that's all I'm saying. Don't make guys are being critiqued for what they do.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: The narrative around Wembanyama creates an unfair expectation of perfection
quotes.excerpt: In our head, we have this classy French figure where he's just different.
quotes.quote: In our head, we have this classy French figure where he's just different. He changes with monks, he reads books, he turns his phone off, but then you don't shake hands. I mean, I think the problem is he's just a human. You're so responsible, mature for 22 years old, and you play different, your years, you're way more mature and wise than your age, but then you do things like this and like, oh he's 22.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's reaction was simply frustration after a tough series
quotes.excerpt: That just means he was upset in that moment and he didn't handle it.
quotes.quote: That just means he was upset in that moment and he didn't handle it.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Beadle argues against the performative nature of post-game handshakes
quotes.excerpt: I've always thought it was a performative, fraudulent part of professional sports.
quotes.quote: I've always thought it was a performative, fraudulent part of professional sports because I know damn good and well half y'all don't like the other half and I don't know why we're pretending like all of a sudden we're buds.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Professionalism in sports requires respecting opponents despite personal feelings
quotes.excerpt: We watch boxing and UFC, these guys talk about each other's families trash.
quotes.quote: We watch boxing and UFC, these guys talk about each other's families trash. I knock your whole head off and I'm still going to shake your hand and give you a hug when it's done because this is what we do. We are competing, we feed our families, and we are professionals at the end of the day. We're not little boys no more where we can just pout and run off. Like you have to stand in the, all the credit that you want to be the face of the league, you have to have that, you have to carry that responsibility.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Consistent unprofessional behavior in playoffs warrants proper critique
quotes.excerpt: It's always Draymond Green, right? But if all of these things happen consecutively and inconsistently.
quotes.quote: It's always Draymond Green, right? But if all of these things happen consecutively and inconsistently in the finals or the playoffs, it's going to be a level of critique that we've never seen before. So when he does it, give him his proper due. That's all I'm saying, give him his proper due.
